subject: Rapid-connect MAP: POC activation cadence & network prerequisites
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@pulselink.io>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: netops@pulselink.io
Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2029 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Rapid-connect POC: timeline + network questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. Our engineering and security leads pushed for a short mutual action plan so we can hit an internal deadline two weeks after kickoff. High level asks: 1) How quickly can Redwood provide API keys and an org for our QA tenant; 2) What does IP allowlisting look like (static egress addresses or CIDR ranges); 3) Do you support VPC peering to our AWS account for streaming data (we need to route traffic to our sandbox VPC)?

We'd like a simple checklist or cadence we can share with Procurement + NetOps. Can you propose a conservative timeline and list of owners?

Cheers,
Asha Patel
Head of Product Operations
Pulselink Therapeutics

--
Pulselink IT: netops@pulselink.io (included for network details)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@pulselink.io>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 13 Jul 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rapid-connect POC: timeline + network questions

Hi Asha — really glad the demo was helpful. Attached is a first-pass "Rapid-connect MAP" (see rapid-connect-MAP-v1.xlsx) and a short network stub (pulselink-network-drawing.pdf) that outlines the minimal prerequisites. Summary below for quick visibility: 

- Org + API keys: Redwood can provision a dedicated org and seed API keys within 48 business hours after receiving the signed MSA/PO (or after the PO exception as agreed). We will issue a scoped API key for the QA tenant and a rotating service key for CI.

- IP allowlist: For hosted evaluation we publish a small set of egress CIDR blocks (three /24s) listed in the attachment. If you prefer an explicit static NAT IP per request, we can accommodate on Dedicated lanes but that requires a reserved capacity agreement.

- VPC peering: We do support AWS VPC peering into a sandbox VPC. NetOps will need to share a peering request (VPC ID, account ID, preferred routing table). Expect a 3-5 business day lead time for peering validation and route propagation during the POC.

Suggested 2-week activation cadence (conservative):
1) Day 0-1: Mutual signoff on MAP and PO submission (Asha / Pulselink Procurement + Soojin);
2) Day 1-3: Redwood provisions org, initial API keys, and sandbox test account (Sóojin / Marissa);
3) Day 3-6: NetOps completes IP allowlist confirmation and test connectivity (Pulselink NetOps);
4) Day 4-8: VPC peering test window and sample inference run (Pulselink NetOps + Rishi);
5) Day 8-14: Performance smoke tests and runbook handoff, success criteria sign-off.

I've flagged owners in the attached MAP sheet and added a small checklist of required artifacts (signed MAP, PO, peering request, firewall rules, test prompt set). For operational reasons we request Pulselink share a single Slack channel or a jumpbox user so our infra team can triage during the peering window.

Next steps: I can 1) send a clean MAP for signature, 2) schedule a 30-min kickoff with NetOps & Security next week, or 3) loop in Procurement only after you confirm the approach. Which do you prefer?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: rapid-connect-MAP-v1.xlsx (MAP with owners & timeline), pulselink-network-drawing.pdf (diagram), redwood-api-quickkey-stub.txt (example header payload)

> On Fri, 12 Jul 2029, Asha Patel <asha.patel@pulselink.io> wrote:
> > Thanks again for the demo...

From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@pulselink.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: netops@pulselink.io
Date: Sun, 14 Jul 2029 10:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Rapid-connect POC: timeline + network questions

Soojin — this is great, thanks. I reviewed the MAP and have two quick clarifications from NetOps: 

1) The NetOps team prefers explicit IPs rather than CIDRs for their firewall program; can Redwood provide a small set of static egress NAT IPs for the evaluation (even if they rotate weekly)?
2) For VPC peering, they asked whether the peering can be limited to a single subnet and limited routes (no broad 0.0.0.0/0). Our security team wants to avoid broad route propagation during the POC.

Procurement also asked for an abbreviated statement of work with clear deliverables and acceptance criteria so they can clear the PO internally. If you can provide that, we can likely submit the PO by Day 1.

I'll do a quick sync with NetOps later today and confirm the peering details. Can you prepare the SOW + a version of the MAP that includes the explicit NAT IPs as an option?

Cheers,
Asha

--
Pulselink NetOps will follow up with peering params once we confirm the sandbox VPC details.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@pulselink.io>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, netops@pulselink.io
Date: Sun, 14 Jul 2029 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rapid-connect POC: timeline + network questions

Thanks Asha — totally understand the NetOps ask. We can offer two options and will surface both in the SOW/MAP: 

Option A (fastest, hosted evaluation): Redwood supplies three static NAT IPs dedicated to Pulselink’s sandbox for the POC window. These IPs are assigned via our egress NAT pool and will be used for allowlisting. They may rotate only under emergency maintenance but we commit to advance notice. No VPC peering required for this option.

Option B (direct peering, restricted scope): VPC peering established with route-filtering to accept only the Pulselink sandbox subnet (we will add a restricted route table entry on our side). Peering validation requires Pulselink to provide: account ID, VPC ID, subnet CIDR to accept, and preferred propagation window. Route restrictions will be applied to avoid broad propagation. Estimated time: 3-5 business days to validate and test.

I'll attach a short SOW draft to the HubSpot deal and to the Drive link above by EOD — it will include acceptance criteria (connectivity test, 1k token/second smoke run, and runbook handoff). Rishi will be our technical lead for the peering validation and will post an operational checklist to the shared Drive.

If Pulselink confirms Option A we can begin Day 0 as soon as we receive a signed MAP and PO (we can then provision API keys within 48 business hours). If you prefer Option B, we'll need the peering params and a preferred test window so Rishi can slot it.

I'll schedule the 30-min kickoff for Tue morning PST unless you prefer a different time.

Best,
Sóojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

> Attachment notes: final SOW and MAP (two-option appendix) will be uploaded to the HubSpot deal and to the shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/drive/poc/PL-map-v1
